summary: Ripretinib (Qinlock) is indicated for advanced GIST after 3+ prior kinase inhibitors including imatinib. As a switch-control inhibitor it locks KIT/PDGFRA in the inactive conformation, covering a broad range of primary and secondary resistance mutations. Distinctive toxicities are alopecia, palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia, myalgia, hypertension, cardiac dysfunction (LVEF monitoring) and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: Advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumour after prior treatment with 3 or more kinase inhibitors, including imatinib

dosage.d: 150 mg once daily continuously (may increase to 150 mg BID on progression per labeling)
dosage.t: With or without food at the same time daily; swallow whole
dosage.n: Hold/reduce for grade 3+ PPES, hypertension or arthralgia; assess LVEF if cardiac symptoms

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Ripretinib is a switch-control (switch-pocket) inhibitor that binds both the switch pocket and activation loop of KIT and PDGFRA, locking the kinases in the inactive state and blocking signalling across a broad spectrum of primary and drug-resistant secondary mutations.
preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

emergency: Chest pain or severe breathlessness (cardiac) - seek emergency care
Blistering hand-foot reaction preventing walking or hand use - seek urgent care

monitoring: LVEF assessment if cardiac symptoms develop
counsel: Hair loss is common and usually reversible; hand-foot redness/peeling needs early reporting and dose pauses
Report muscle/joint pain that limits movement
Report swelling, breathlessness or chest discomfort
Check blood pressure as instructed; tell the team about new medicines; use contraception
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Approximately 15 hours (once-daily dosing; active metabolite similar)
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: Switch-pocket mechanism covers heterogeneous secondary KIT mutations that defeat sequential type II TKIs
Dose escalation to BID on progression is labeling-recognised (INVICTUS progression cohort)
Alopecia + PPES is the counselling signature - set expectations early
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. Take as soon as remembered on the same day; if the next dose is near, skip; do not double. On BID escalation follow the same rule per dose.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
